items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: Clark Terry was — Clark and Snooky were the greatest disciples that ever came along.

ctx.x: When did that start, in the early ‘60s was it?

Well it started about the time that I brought Clark in, because they used to spit on me when I first became music director. We had no men of color in the orchestra. Two Italians, they said they were colored. But seriously, and during the very — when the movement was very strong they really were rough on me at NBC and I tried to explain to them that it took time and that I had to have people who would fit. Clark Terry was — Clark and Snooky were the greatest disciples that ever came along. But Clark and Doc didn’t…

— what was it — Doc said Clark played out of tune and Clark said Doc had no tune. So they had some colloquial like that. But that was the beginning of the so-called integration. It’s strange how we talk about it now that it’s gone by the board. It was very rough for me at one time though. And I didn’t know any better.
